input: Simulate a build pipeline: 1) Check that /src/main.c and /src/utils.c exist, 2) 'Compile' each .c file by copying it to /build/ with a .o extension and prepending '// compiled', 3) 'Link' by concatenating all .o files into /build/program with a '// linked' header, 4) 'Package' by creating a tar.gz of /build/ at /dist/release.tar.gz. Print status for each stage. If any stage fails, stop and report the error.

transcript.final_response:
All four stages passed.

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| 1. Check | `/src/main.c` and `/src/utils.c` both exist. |
| 2. Compile | Created `/build/main.o` and `/build/utils.o`, each starting with `// compiled`. |
| 3. Link | Created `/build/program`, which starts with `// linked` followed by both `.o` files. |
| 4. Package | Created `/dist/release.tar.gz`, which contains `build/`, `build/program`, `build/main.o` and `build/utils.o`. |

The script stops and reports the stage name if any step fails, but no step failed.
tool_calls:
set -e
fail(){ echo "FAILED at stage: $1 - $2"; exit 1; }

echo "== Stage 1: Check sources =="
for f in /src/main.c /src/utils.c; do [ -f "$f" ] || fail "check" "$f missing"; done
echo "OK: sources found"

echo "== Stage 2: Compile =="
mkdir -p /build || fail compile "mkdir"
for f in /src/*.c; do
  o=/build/$(basename "${f%.c}").o
  { echo "// compiled"; cat "$f"; } > "$o" || fail compile "$f"
  echo "compiled $f -> $o"
done

echo "== Stage 3: Link =="
{ echo "// linked"; cat /build/*.o; } > /build/program || fail link "concat"
echo "linked -> /build/program"

echo "== Stage 4: Package =="
mkdir -p /dist || fail package "mkdir"
tar -czf /dist/release.tar.gz -C / build || fail package "tar"
echo "packaged -> /dist/release.tar.gz"
tar -tzf /dist/release.tar.gz
echo; echo "--- /build/program ---"; cat /build/program
